name: Dhaka University Students
contribution: Dhaka University students organized debates, meetings, processions, and strikes that carried the Language Movement from campus politics into public protest.
context: Between 1948 and 1952, the campus became a key site for opposition to the attempt to impose Urdu as Pakistan’s sole state language. Students challenged restrictions including Section 144 and joined wider civic mobilization.
impact: Their collective action helped turn language rights into a mass political demand and made the movement a foundational chapter in East Bengal’s later democratic and nationalist history.
highlight: The student collective that helped move the Language Movement from Dhaka University into a mass public struggle.
seoTitle: Dhaka University Students and the Language Movement
seoDescription: Learn how Dhaka University students organized the 1948–1952 Language Movement and turned the demand for Bengali language rights into mass political action.
shortAnswer: Dhaka University students were central organizers of the Language Movement, helping turn Bengali language rights into a mass public and political demand.
